Everything a pixel artist needs

Built to feel like Aseprite, extended where it matters. One project file for sprites, animations, tilemaps, and AI operations.

Pixel-perfect editing core

If an Aseprite user opens Pixhaus and feels lost, the editing layer has failed. The pixel-art surface is ground-truth-equivalent before anything AI ships on top.

Pencil, eraser, fill, line, rectangle, ellipse

All standard pixel tools with pixel-perfect stroke mode.

Dither brush and pattern stamp

Checker, Bayer 8x8, and custom pattern brushes for classic dithering.

Selection: marquee, lasso, magic wand, color range

With boolean ops (union, intersect, subtract, xor) and expand/contract.

Flip, scale, rotate (RotSprite)

Pixel-aware RotSprite algorithm for integer rotations. No blurring.

Indexed-color discipline

Full palette workflow — palette-swaps, color cycling, transparent index.

.aseprite and .psd file support

Read and write .aseprite directly. Import .psd for migration.

Frame animation

Timeline that includes tilemaps and animated tiles, not just sprite layers.

Frame timeline with tags and loop direction

Named frame ranges with forward / reverse / pingpong / once loop modes.

Onion skin overlay

Previous and next frames at configurable opacity, tinted for direction.

Layer groups with blend modes

Full blend mode set (Normal, Multiply, Screen, Overlay, and 18 more).

Sprite sheet export (PNG + JSON)

Aseprite-compatible JSON schema — works with existing Unity importers.

Animated GIF, WebP, and MP4 export

Palette quantization, dithering, loop count, configurable frame timing.

Unlimited undo with branch history

Branching undo tree preserves redo branches across edit paths.

Tilemaps as first-class layers

Closing the Aseprite–Tiled split. Tileset and tilemap in the same project as the sprites they display.

Tilemap layer type

Tileset definition, per-cell tile data, rotation and flip flags — all inside the .pixhaus project.

Autotile rules

16-tile Wang corner-blob, 47-tile Wang edge-blob, and rule-based custom sets.

Animated tiles

Water, lava, conveyor belts — tiles cycle independently of the sprite timeline.

Tile properties

Per-tile collision shape, animation timing, autotile group membership.

TMX export for Tiled

SuperTiled2Unity-compatible .tmx + tileset PNG for Unity tilemap pipelines.

In-editor rule tile editor

Visual editor for custom autotile rules — no separate Tiled session required.

AI verbs

Commands that run inside the canvas with your palette, your layers, and your style references as automatic context. Not a side panel. Not a separate generator. Each verb produces a preview layer you accept, edit, or discard — the artist's brush stays in the artist's hand.

Bring your own API key (Anthropic, OpenAI, Replicate, Stability) or run locally with Ollama and ComfyUI. No backend is mandatory.

Inbetween

Generate intermediate frames between two key frames, palette-locked. Uses frame-interpolation models conditioned on source frames.

Continue

Predict the next 1–3 frames given the last N, consistent with motion and style.

Extend

Generate 4-direction or 8-direction views from a single sprite. Renders from synthesized geometry, snaps to palette.

Variant

Palette swaps, equipment overlays, expression sets — as derived layers from a base sprite.

Cleanup

Snap generated or imported sprites to the active palette, remove sub-pixel anti-aliasing, fix pivot drift across frames.

Tile

Generate a 47-tile blob autotile set from 1–3 example transitions, with rules pre-configured.

Critique

Vision-language analysis: pose continuity errors, palette violations, missing frames, pivot drift, style inconsistency — surfaced as a clickable issue list.

Project style learning

Train a per-project LoRA from existing layers. Subsequent verbs use it as a style reference automatically.

Conversational editing

Natural language driving multi-step editor commands. Plans the command sequence, previews it, commits on accept.

Motion from video

Extract pose timing from a reference video into the timeline as keyframe markers and rough silhouettes.

Auto-mesh deformation

Derive a no-bones deformation rig from a single sprite — Live2D-style results without explicit skeleton work.

Audio-driven timing

Beat detection and lip-sync to drive animation frame timing from audio clips.

Tileset from description

Generate a complete autotile-compatible tileset from a text prompt.

Sketch finishing

Refine rough silhouettes and gesture poses into finished sprites in your project's learned style.

Unity integration

The first-party Unity package reads Pixhaus exports cleanly, with better pivot and animation tag handling than third-party Aseprite importers.

Pixhaus Unity importer (UPM)

OpenUPM-compatible package. Auto-slices, generates AnimationClips per frame tag, sets pivots.

SpriteAtlas batching

Multiple imported sprite sheets are combined into a SpriteAtlas automatically.

Tilemap support

Imports TMX exports into Unity's Tilemap system with TileBase assets for each tile.

Unity 2022.3 LTS + Unity 6

Minimum Unity 2022.3 LTS; Unity 6 is the primary test target.

Scripting and plugins

Lua scripting with an Aseprite-compatible API surface so existing scripts have a migration path. Plugins reach further: custom UI panels, custom tools, custom AI verbs.

Lua scripting (Lua 5.4)

Hot-reload. The app global mirrors Aseprite's API. Community scripts port with minimal changes.

WASM plugins via extism

Pre-compile plugins in any language that targets WASM. Sandboxed, no filesystem access outside the project.

Custom UI panels

Plugins can register panels, toolbars, and dialog UIs — not just data transforms.

Custom AI verbs

Register your own verb that calls any backend. The verb protocol is the extension point.
